page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.small is an entry-level virtual server belonging to the Shared family, provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. Hardware resources include 1 dedicated vCPU mapped to a single physical core on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU is built on the x86_64 architecture and includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, BMI2, and AES. Memory capacity is fixed at 2.0 GB, providing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. This server includes no integrated local storage, no attached GPU hardware, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the instance in the lowest decile across general server performance tiers due to its single-thread limitations. The stress-ng CPU test recorded 1026.39 points in both single-core and multi-core evaluations. In PassMark tests, the CPU attained an overall score of 1291.58, with 1188.1 in extended instructions, 401.31 in encryption, and 176.92 in physics calculations. The memory subsystem achieved a PassMark memory score of 673.93, delivering 76.38 GB/sec in small-block cached reads, while large-block uncached memory operations yielded 8.4 GB/sec read and 6.9 GB/sec write bandwidth. Compression benchmarks registered single-threaded throughput of 18.42 GB/sec for gzip and 6.62 GB/sec for bzip3 decompression.

Application-level measurements showed 1.35 million Redis SET operations per second, a PassMark database score of 532.63, and 0.91 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. The minimal hardware footprint provides qualitative cost efficiency for simple operations that do not saturate CPU cycles. However, the lack of local disk storage and single-core ceiling restrict its use in multi-threaded computation or high-concurrency environments. Appropriate workloads include lightweight microservices, low-traffic web proxies, basic development testbeds, task schedulers, and small administrative utilities.

Benchmark testing reflects its single-core baseline, registering a PassMark CPU score of 1291.58, a stress-ng score of 1026.39, and uncached read memory bandwidth of 8.4 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 10 percent of evaluated systems.
